quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, how should you adjust for the added weight?

options.text: Ride slower than usual.
Stay closer to the vehicle ahead than you normally would.
Ride faster than usual.
Brake later than you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. This extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Ride slower, start braking earlier, leave more space between you and other vehicles, and look for larger gaps when entering or merging with traffic.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It protects only your eyes.
It protects your entire face.
It works less well than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your entire face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield alone does not give enough protection.

questions.question: At what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is a person legally intoxicated?

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.1 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 percent or higher means a person is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to ride while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: What do studies show about motorcycles with headlights on during the day?

options.text: They are harder to see than other vehicles.
Other drivers see them better than when the headlight is off.
Other drivers get confused.
They are less safe than with the headlight off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers see them better than when the headlight is off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever you ride. A motorcycle with its headlight on during the day is twice as likely to be noticed by other drivers.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign, what should you do?

options.text: Stop at the stop sign and proceed through.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to see better.
Stop at the stop sign, then edge forward to see cross traffic.
Drive through without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign, then edge forward to see cross traffic.
questions.explanation: Stop where the stop sign or line indicates. Then edge forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean your body forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: How does a three-wheeled motorcycle handle curves?

options.text: The same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
It should not be used on curves.
It should use the shoulder when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or motorcycle with a sidecar handles curves very differently from a regular two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you do if another vehicle is following you too closely?

options.text: Speed up.
Move onto the shoulder.
Let the other driver pass you.
Exit the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other driver pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them ahead of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may increase danger by making them tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: If someone drinks 7 alcoholic drinks in 3 hours, how many drinks will likely be in their system 3 hours after their last drink? (The body removes about 1 drink per hour.)

options.text: Two
Three
Four
Five

questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: To estimate drinks remaining in a person's system, subtract the hours since their last drink from the total drinks consumed. For example: 7 drinks consumed minus 6 hours elapsed (3 hours drinking plus 3 hours after) leaves 4 drinks remaining.

questions.question: When riding in a group and passing another vehicle, what is the best way?

options.text: One rider completes their pass before the next rider begins.
Several group members pass at the same time.
The last rider waves to signal no more motorcycles are coming.
Pass in a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: One rider completes their pass before the next rider begins.
questions.explanation: In a group, riders should pass one at a time. Each rider should finish their pass and return to the group formation before the next rider begins to pass.

questions.question: Which option does NOT help prevent a friend from driving while intoxicated?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Keep them busy with activities while they sober up.
Have them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
Get other friends to help stop them from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
questions.explanation: To prevent drunk driving, arrange another way home, keep them busy with other activities, use any reason to keep them from leaving, and get friends to help. Waiting 15 minutes after drinking does not reduce intoxication enough to make driving safe.

questions.question: When alcohol enters the bloodstream and reaches the brain, what is affected first?

options.text: Judgment
Speech
Balance
Vision

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment and decision-making before you reach the legal blood alcohol limit.

questions.question: Convex mirrors make cars look:

options.text: Larger.
Farther away.
Faster.
Narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give you a wider view of the road. However, they make objects appear farther away than they actually are.

questions.question: Which item provides a rider with the best protection?

options.text: Goggles
A face shield
A windshield
Eyeglasses

questions.correctAnswerText: A face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: When getting ready to pass another vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Not signal your intentions, as that may distract the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When passing on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane. Signal your intentions and check for traffic. Pass when it is safe, then signal and return to your original lane.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Read books about carrying passengers.
Practice riding on an empty road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the shoulder of a road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on an empty road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger in traffic, practice on a quiet road. This helps you get used to how your motorcycle handles with the extra weight.

questions.question: When choosing clothes for riding, which is not a good choice?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles
Gloves made of leather
A baseball cap to cover your hair

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves. A baseball cap does not provide protection.

questions.question: An experienced rider:

options.text: Changes positions within their lane as conditions change.
Stays in one portion of a lane at all times.
Weaves within the lane to be more visible.
Travels only on the oily portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes positions within their lane as conditions change.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle rider has three lane position options. The rider should choose whichever position is safest based on the road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: The front brake should:

options.text: Not be used by inexperienced riders.
Be used by itself.
Occasionally assist the rear brake.
Be used together with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes together every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which is not a type of protective riding gear?

options.text: A leather jacket
Boots that go above the ankle
Hearing protection
Pants made of a soft material

questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of a soft material
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a jacket and pants made of leather or sturdy material, footwear that covers and supports your ankles, and hearing protection. Soft material pants do not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: If carrying a load in a sidecar, the motorcycle's stopping distance:

options.text: May be increased.
May be decreased.
Is not a concern.
Will be similar to a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be increased.
questions.explanation: Adding a load increases the motorcycle's weight and inertia, which may increase stopping distance. Start slowing down and stopping earlier when carrying a load or passenger.
